gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-001 directly identifies the false universal claim that every vertically closed form has the nearest-neighbour representation, explains the mismatch with arbitrary prolongation shifts, and proposes restricting the converse to the standard subclass.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both identify the unjustified assertion that arbitrary vertically closed or multisymplectic forms can be represented by the restricted nearest-neighbour expression in eq:multiform, despite general forms allowing arbitrary shift indices.

component_coverage.gold_component: The universal nearest-neighbour representation claim is false for general vertically closed forms on the prolongation space; arbitrary shift coordinates are allowed and the standard expression is only a restricted subclass.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction states the universal standard-form claim, contrasts its restricted shifted-variable structure with arbitrary multi-index vertical basis forms, gives a counterexample, and supplies the appropriate restriction of the converse statement.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-002 directly identifies that the construction proves only that original-system solutions satisfy the constructed Euler–Lagrange equations, not the converse, so solution-set equivalence and the equivalent-Lagrangian claim are unsupported.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both identify the failure of the construction to establish equality of the original and Euler–Lagrange solution sets: only the implication from original solutions to Euler–Lagrange solutions is shown, while additional Euler–Lagrange solutions may exist.

component_coverage.gold_component: The claimed equivalence of the original multisymplectic system and the constructed Euler–Lagrange system is unsupported because only one-way solution inclusion is established and the latter system may admit additional solutions.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly distinguishes the proved implication from the missing converse, identifies possible additional solutions, and proposes weakening the equivalence claim to a one-way associated-Lagrangian statement.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold issue concerns the domain of definition of a logarithmic Hamiltonian and its Euler–Lagrange formula, requiring a positive second component. ISSUE-002 instead concerns a missing converse implication between solution sets and contains no diagnosis of the Hamiltonian's domain or logarithm.
